s.d: A common way to describe ordinary chicken eggs on a breakfast menu, especially in expensive restaurants and hotels.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see fresh, country, eggs.
e: Every Saturday a farmer came to our door selling fresh country eggs from his big round basket covered with straw.
He started shipping about half a case of fresh country eggs to my parents every week or two.

s.d: A joke with a punchline implying that the Irish people are stupid.
Something illogical or silly that happened in Ireland.
Emotionally moved (by), made to feel emotion (by).
e: I was touched that he should remember my birthday.
"They say her Majesty is more touched about these affairs of the Chartists than anything else," said Mr Egerton.

s.d: Slightly mentally deficient; touched in the head.
e: All a bit touched. Mad Fanny and his other sister Mrs Dickinson driving about with scarlet harness.
The girl’s face is dreamy, slow. Touched, the Irish say. Possible that she’s touched.

s.d: To get an erection of the penis.
